topics.name: Modals of deduction (must have, can't have)

options: Don't gives me advice right now.
Not give me advice right now.
Don't give me advice right now.
questions.rule: A negative imperative is Don't + base verb: Don't give.

options: Do it belong to the history book?
Does it belong to the history book?
Does it belongs to the history book?
questions.rule: With it, use Does + base verb: Does it belong? The verb after does never takes -s.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: A request starts with the base verb: Please listen ... and do not interrupt.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After a modal, use the base form: must have + past participle, never must has.

questions.before: Meera loves mobile games, and so
questions.rule: So + helper + subject agrees with a positive idea. Loves needs does, and her brother is singular.

questions.after: do you think about the new traffic signal?
questions.rule: We ask for an opinion with What do you think about ...? (We say How do you feel, but What do you think.)
A negative command: Don't + base verb, then the time clause: while I am speaking.

chat: I think cricket is more fun than football.
options: I am totally agree with you.
questions.rule: Agree is a verb, so no am before it, and with I it has no -s: I totally agree.
A request is reported with requested + object + to + base verb: requested me to listen.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: After Don't, use the base verb: Don't start, don't tell.

questions.prompt: The road is wet this morning. Which sentence is correct?
options: It must have rained last night.
It must has rained last night.
It must have rain last night.
questions.rule: A sure guess about the past: must have + past participle: must have rained.

options: I don't like loud TV shows, and neither do my sister.
I don't like loud TV shows, and neither my sister does.
I don't like loud TV shows, and neither does my sister.
questions.rule: Neither + helper + subject agrees with a negative idea. My sister is singular: neither does my sister.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: In a question with did, the main verb stays in the base form: did you start?

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: A reported command uses told + object + to + base verb: told the players to listen.

questions.after: worry; I can solve this problem myself.
questions.rule: A negative request is Please don't + base verb. Doesn't is not used in imperatives.
A yes/no question: Do + subject + base verb: Do you agree with ...?

chat: I am thinking of something from our science book. Guess!
options: Is it a plant or a animal?
Are it a plant or an animal?
Is it a plant or an animal?
questions.rule: It takes is, and animal starts with a vowel sound, so we say an animal.

chat: The new bus route is very useful.
options: I suppose so, but it are too crowded.
I suppose so, but it is too crowded.
I suppose so, but it too crowded.
questions.rule: Every clause needs a verb, and it takes is: it is too crowded.

questions.source: Mother said to Neha, "Don't over-protect your little brother."
options: Mother told Neha not to over-protect your little brother.
Mother told Neha don't over-protect her little brother.
Mother told Neha not to over-protect her little brother.
questions.rule: Don't becomes not to + base verb, and your changes to her for Neha.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: Use must have / might have + past participle: must have forgotten, might have died.

options: She can't have heard the bell; she was wearing headphones.
She can't have hear the bell; she was wearing headphones.
She can't has heard the bell; she was wearing headphones.
questions.rule: A sure 'no' about the past: can't have + past participle: can't have heard.

options: The speaker asked us that wait for our turn.
The speaker asked us waiting for our turn.
The speaker asked us to wait for our turn.
questions.rule: A reported request: asked + object + to + base verb: asked us to wait.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The short answer copies the helper of the first verb. Hate (simple present) needs do: so do I.
Nobody is negative, so the tag is positive, and it uses they: do they?
A suggestion with Let's always takes the tag shall we?

questions.prompt: Make a sure guess about the past.
questions.rule: must have + past participle (felt) shows we are sure about the past.

chat: Rohan didn't come to the match today.
questions.rule: must have + past participle: must have been. After must we never use had.

chat: What did your father say about the phone?
options: He told me to not using it after nine o'clock.
He told me don't use it after nine o'clock.
He told me not to use it after nine o'clock.
questions.rule: A reported 'don't' order: told + object + not to + base verb: told me not to use.

options: Does the leader gives truthful answers?
Does the leader give truthful answers?
Is the leader give truthful answers?
questions.rule: Simple present question: Does + subject + base verb. The -s moves to does: Does the leader give?

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: These apps is plural, so use are. After Does, use the base verb: believe.

options: She must have been cry before we arrived.
She must have been crying before we arrived.
She must have been crying before we had arrive.
questions.rule: must have been + -ing guesses about an ongoing past action; before we arrived uses the simple past.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After don't in an imperative, use the base verb: Please don't tell me.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The short answer copies the helper: has finished ... so has Meera.
Present perfect continuous: have + been + -ing. With you, use have: have you been writing?

questions.prompt: Ask a question that guesses about the past.
questions.rule: Wh-word + must have + past participle: What must have happened ...?

chat: Mobile phones should be banned in school.
options: Not necessarily. Some students uses them for learning.
Not necessarily. Some students use them for learning.
Not necessarily. Some student use them for learning.
questions.rule: Some + plural noun (students) takes a plural verb without -s: use.

chat: I tried to send you a photo, but it didn't work.
options: Don't worry, Grandpa. Let me show you how to do it.
Don't worry, Grandpa. Let me shows you how to do it.
Don't worry, Grandpa. Let me to show you how to do it.
questions.rule: Let + object + base verb, with no to and no -s: Let me show you.

questions.source: The teacher said, "Students, form groups of six."
options: The teacher ordered the students to formed groups of six.
The teacher ordered the students that form groups of six.
The teacher ordered the students to form groups of six.
questions.rule: A command is reported with ordered + object + to + base verb: ordered the students to form.

questions.prompt: Change into an interrogative sentence without changing the meaning.
questions.rule: A positive statement becomes a negative question: Isn't advice cheap? The helper is moves to the front once.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: After to, use the base verb: to listen more and talk less, to finish.

options: They can't have went far; their bikes are still outside the gate.
They can't have go far; their bikes are still outside the gate.
They can't have gone far; their bikes are still outside the gate.
questions.rule: can't have + past participle. The past participle of go is gone, not went.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Has never seen is present perfect, so the reply copies it with I: neither have I.

questions.after: taken my notebook; it isn't in my bag.
questions.rule: A modal is followed by the base form: must have taken.
A reported question uses statement word order: what we had, not question order.
In a reported question, the subject comes before the verb: why I was, not why was I.

chat: The window is broken and there is a cricket ball on the floor.
Who do you think did it?
options: The boys next door must have been play cricket.
The boys next door must have been playing cricket.
The boys next door must been playing cricket.
questions.rule: A guess about an ongoing past action: must have been + -ing: must have been playing.

questions.source: He said to me, "Please don't talk; just hear me."
options: He requested me not to talk but just to hear him.
He requested me not to talk but just to hear me.
He requested me to not talking but just hear him.
questions.rule: Please becomes requested; don't talk becomes not to talk; the speaker's me becomes him.

questions.source: Ravi asked me, "Do you agree with my opinion?"
options: Ravi asked me if did I agree with his opinion.
Ravi asked me if I agreed with his opinion.
Ravi asked me if I agreed with my opinion.
questions.rule: A yes/no question is reported with if + statement order; the tense moves back (agreed) and my becomes his.

questions.source: The speaker does not want advice. He does not want pity either.
options: The speaker wants neither advice or pity.
The speaker wants neither advice nor pity.
The speaker does not want neither advice nor pity.
questions.rule: Neither always pairs with nor, and it is already negative, so we do not add not.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this message.
questions.rule: don't + base verb (give); a patient listener is singular (is); a gerund subject (listening ...) takes a singular verb (makes).
